title: CV
text:
Data scientist and developer with 6+ years building data infrastructure for the Neotoma Paleoecology Database, a global paleoecology software ecosystem. I maintain the database, design API endpoints, and automate pipelines on AWS. I publish open-source packages that let scientists access and contribute data at scale, and I teach Python and machine learning, making complex data concepts approachable for non-technical audiences.
Vancouver area, BC, Canada ·  s.dominguez@ht-data.com

title: CV
text:
Experience

Data Scientist II
University of Wisconsin–Madison (remote) · Apr 2026 to present

Evolve Neotoma’s PostgreSQL schema to support structurally new data types such as ancient and environmental DNA (aeDNA) and speleothems, keeping the database normalized while broadening what the research community can store.
Build GitHub Actions pipelines that automate database-to-AWS workflows, including DOI minting and automated statistical summary reports.
Develop data-download pipelines that transform database records into standardized community formats such as FAIRe, improving interoperability and reuse.
Add ORCID-based authentication to Neotoma, so researchers can sign in securely with their existing ORCID identities.
Implement embargoes for sensitive data using row-level security and access controls, in line with data governance and privacy policies.
Write technical sections for grant proposals supporting new Neotoma initiatives.



Data Scientist I
University of Wisconsin–Madison (remote) · May 2020 to Apr 2026

Developed and published neotoma2, an open-source R package on CRAN that gives researchers programmatic access to Neotoma (~5,000 downloads in the past year).
Built DataBUS, a Python system that automates bulk ingestion into Neotoma, enabling the upload of 6,087 new datasets from 62 countries in a single year.
Built a Docker image bundling PostgreSQL/PostGIS with Neotoma’s public data snapshot, so geoscientists can run the full database locally without a difficult PostGIS installation.
Extended Neotoma’s API to expose new data fields researchers needed, then surfaced them in neotoma2, working end to end from the API layer to the user-facing tool.
Led hands-on workshops in Prague, Rome, Berlin, Cape Town, and Madison, and presented at international conferences including INQUA, AGU, and ESIP. See talks & workshops →



Data Science Course Coordinator, Key Capabilities in Data Science Certificate
University of British Columbia, Vancouver · Sep 2020 to present

Teach Python programming and machine learning to 1,000+ working professionals, with consistently positive student evaluations.
Build and run online course environments in Canvas and Piazza, and keep course materials current.
Mentored three new facilitators in effective teaching practices.



Coding Instructor
Lighthouse Labs (remote) · Aug 2020 to Aug 2025

Designed and delivered bootcamp lessons in Python, statistics, data visualization, SQL, and natural language processing.
Provided live instruction with hands-on, one-on-one support.



Actuarial Analyst
AXA Insurance, Mexico City · Nov 2010 to Apr 2014

Built reserve-calculation models in SQL and shell scripting for health-insurance products, working with sensitive healthcare data under strict privacy controls.
Optimized the reserve-recalculation pipeline, cutting up to 3.5 hours of compute time per run.
Cleaned and engineered large datasets (5M+ rows) and presented results to executives and head actuaries.

title: Socorro Dominguez Vidaña
text:
Hi, I’m Socorro! I’m a data scientist based in the Vancouver area with more than six years of experience building data infrastructure for science. I care about making research data open, reliable, and easy to reuse, and about helping people reach their Eureka moments when they learn to work with it.
Most of my work happens around the Neotoma Paleoecology Database, a free, community-curated resource for fossil and environmental records from the last few million years. I maintain the database, design its API endpoints, and automate pipelines on AWS. I also build the open-source tools that let scientists access and contribute data at scale, and I teach Python and machine learning to working professionals.


 Data infrastructure
PostgreSQL schema design, public APIs, cloud pipelines, ORCID sign-in, and automated DOIs for open research data.


 Open software
Author of the neotoma2 R package and the DataBUS upload toolkit. See all software →


 Teaching
Python and machine learning for 1,000+ professionals, plus workshops on four continents. See talks & workshops →


If I’m not coding, I’m most likely practicing Chinese martial arts.

title: Consulting
text: I help research groups and organizations get more out of their data, from messy spreadsheets to production databases.

title: Consulting
text:
What I can help with

Research data infrastructure: PostgreSQL database design and administration, public APIs, cloud hosting, and automated DOIs.
Data pipelines and quality: validation workflows, bulk uploads, and reproducible pipelines that catch problems before they spread.
Open research software: R and Python packages, from first prototype to CRAN release and peer review.
FAIR data: making datasets findable and reusable with metadata standards like FAIRe.
Training: hands-on workshops and courses in R, Python, and data science. I’ve mentored over 1,000 students and taught workshops in English and Spanish.

title: Software
text: Open-source tools I’ve built or co-built, mostly for the Neotoma Paleoecology Database community. Everything here is free to use.

title: Software
text:
neotoma2
An R package for finding, downloading, and analyzing data from the Neotoma Paleoecology Database. It follows a tidyverse-style approach, so Neotoma records drop straight into your usual R workflows.

 CRAN (install.packages("neotoma2"))
 Peer reviewed in the Journal of Open Source Software (2023)
 Documentation and tutorials
 Source code

title: Software
text:
DataBUS
A toolkit that validates and bulk-uploads community datasets into Neotoma. Every file is checked against the Neotoma data model before upload, and uploads run as a single all-or-nothing transaction, so a site is never left half-loaded. I’ve built DataBUS workflows for ostracode and speleothem (SISAL) data, and I’m currently building one for ancient and environmental DNA.

 Zenodo archive
 Source code

title: Software
text:
neotoma2faire (in development)
Exports ancient and environmental DNA data from the Neotoma APIs into the FAIRe (FAIR eDNA) metadata standard, so eDNA records can be shared in an open, machine-readable format.
